items.description: "It feels like it's unrealistic to want to do a daily snapshot of all S3 data keeping a history of 5 snapshots. Although, I do have 80 Gb available. Regardless I feel like this may need some smarts." — the mirror is incremental. A run over unchanged buckets uploads nothing and leaves no archive folder, and Drive holds the live data plus replaced or deleted objects only, never a full copy per run.
items.rationale: `sync()` is a single `rclone sync rgw:<bucket> mirror:current/<bucket> --backup-dir mirror:archive/<bucket>/<stamp>` per bucket — rclone's own incremental transfer, and `--backup-dir` only ever receives what a sync would otherwise overwrite or delete, so an unchanged bucket produces no archive folder (rclone creates the directory lazily, on first write into it) and `prune()`'s own `lsf --dirs-only` exits 3 ("no archive yet") in that case, confirmed read. The unit suite drives this logic against fake `subprocess.run` calls (10 tests) and P2's done-record additionally reports a local end-to-end run with real rclone v1.75.1 over local dirs (crypt, upload, archive, prune-to-N, a failing bucket) — behavioural evidence, not a lint pass. The first live run (V01) is the remaining empirical confirmation against real Drive/RGW.
evidence: HelmCharts `charts/storage/files/s3-mirror/s3_mirror.py:60-65` (`sync`), `:68-85` (`prune`)
HelmCharts `tests/test_storage_s3_mirror.py` — 10 tests over a fake `subprocess.run`
plan.md P2 record — local end-to-end run with real rclone v1.75.1

items.description: "A sync sounds perfect." — each prd-stage bucket is mirrored by an incremental, encrypted `rclone sync` to the existing Google Drive remote (`gdrive-pieter:Homelab Backups`, HelmCharts `configs/prd/storage/prd/values.yaml:15`), run from the `storage` chart. On Drive, file and folder names and contents are encrypted. Decrypted, the mirror holds `current/<bucket>/<object key path>` as live state and `archive/<bucket>/<run timestamp>/<object key path>` for what each run replaced or deleted (ruling W1).
items.rationale: The CronJob template sets the crypt remote's `RCLONE_CONFIG_MIRROR_REMOTE` from `.Values.s3Mirror.driveRemote` (`gdrive-pieter:Homelab Backups/s3-mirror`), `filename_encryption=standard`, `filename_encoding=base32`, `directory_name_encryption=true`, matching W1 and the runbook exactly. The script's `sync()`/`prune()` write `current/<bucket>/...` and `archive/<bucket>/<stamp>/...` as designed. Live: the CronJob and its ConfigMap-shipped script are deployed in `storage-prd` with these exact env values (confirmed by reading the deployed template source; the mirror's first run — V01 — is the remaining live proof of actual Drive content).

items.description: One fleet-wide, read-only `backup-reader` RGW user, granted per bucket by a provider-attached bucket policy: `backup-reader` exists on prd with the admin capability `buckets=read` and nothing more, owns no bucket and cannot create one. It can list and read every prd-stage bucket, and every write or delete it attempts is refused.
items.rationale: Live-created: `homelab_s3_reader.backup_reader` (IaC/HelmCharts build #6464) completed in 1s with `id=backup-reader`, owning no bucket (the resource carries no `buckets` argument at all). The provider's `CreateUser` call sends exactly `max-buckets=-1, user-caps=buckets=read` (read, `internal/s3reader`) — no bucket-write or bucket-create capability. The bucket policy the grant writes (`internal/s3storage/policy.go:31-34`) names exactly two `Allow` statements — `s3:ListBucket` and `s3:GetObject` — nothing else, and is the bucket's *whole* policy (an in-place `Modifying...`/`Modifications complete` on the owning resource, not a merge), so nothing outside those two actions is ever granted; RGW's default is deny. `client_test.go` pins this exact statement shape. The empirical negative test (`backup-reader`'s key actually gets a 403 on a PUT/DELETE) is the unrun TF_ACC acceptance suite (close-out A2) — not run in this pass, since it needs a scratch bucket and the acceptance harness the doc reserves for the operator.
evidence: internal/s3reader `resource.go`, `client.go` — `max-buckets=-1`, `user-caps=buckets=read`
internal/s3storage `policy.go:31-34` — two `Allow` statements, `s3:ListBucket` + `s3:GetObject` only
internal/s3storage `client_test.go:264-284` — pins the exact statement shape

items.description: A prd-stage bucket the mirror cannot list or read fails the run (the Job fails), never a skip; any rclone error fails the Job.
items.rationale: `prd_buckets()` exits non-zero (`sys.exit`) on a non-2xx admin-API response or an empty bucket list, before any sync starts. Inside the per-bucket loop, `sync`/`prune` raise `CalledProcessError` on any rclone failure (`rclone()` uses `check=True`); `main()` catches it, appends the bucket to `failures` and continues with the rest, then `sys.exit("FAILED buckets: ...")` if `failures` is non-empty — the process exits non-zero, so the Kubernetes Job is marked Failed. Covered by `tests/test_storage_s3_mirror.py`'s failing-bucket case. Not yet exercised live (no run has happened — V01).
evidence: HelmCharts `charts/storage/files/s3-mirror/s3_mirror.py:52-56` (listing failure), `:104-115` (`main`, per-bucket try/except, final `sys.exit`)
HelmCharts `tests/test_storage_s3_mirror.py` — failing-bucket case

items.description: A bucket that disappears from RGW keeps its mirror copy untouched; the job never deletes a whole bucket's mirror.
items.rationale: The script only ever iterates `buckets` returned by `prd_buckets()` (the current RGW listing); nothing in `sync`, `prune` or `main` reads or purges any `mirror:current/<bucket>` or `mirror:archive/<bucket>` tree for a bucket absent from that list. There is no delete/purge call anywhere outside `prune()`'s own per-bucket archive-folder purge, which only ever touches the buckets in that run's `buckets` list.
evidence: HelmCharts `charts/storage/files/s3-mirror/s3_mirror.py:88-115` (`main`) — no code path reachable for a bucket outside the current `prd_buckets()` result

items.description: After each successful sync the mirror keeps the 30 newest archive folders per bucket and prunes the rest. A run that moved nothing leaves no archive folder, so history is counted in changes, not days.
items.rationale: `prune(bucket, keep)` lists `archive/<bucket>` folders (or returns immediately on rclone's "directory not found" exit code 3 — no folder yet), sorts them lexically (the `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` stamp sorts chronologically), and purges every folder but the newest `keep`. `KEEP_ARCHIVES` is `30` in the chart's default values (`charts/storage/values.yaml:43`) and unmodified in prd. `--backup-dir` only creates a folder when a sync moves something (rclone's own behaviour, read in the code comment and confirmed by the local end-to-end run in P2's record), so an unchanged run adds nothing to prune.
evidence: HelmCharts `charts/storage/files/s3-mirror/s3_mirror.py:68-85` (`prune`)
HelmCharts `charts/storage/values.yaml:43` — `keepArchives: 30`
HelmCharts `configs/prd/storage/prd/values.yaml` — no override, so 30 is the deployed value
HelmCharts `tests/test_storage_s3_mirror.py` — prune-to-N test case; P2 record's local rclone e2e run

items.description: A critical Prometheus rule in the production Prometheus release, beside the other rules (HelmCharts `configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:61`), on the mirror job's last successful run. Both edges of ruling D2 hold. One missed night stays quiet, however long the following run takes: the last-successful time is the Job's completion, not its schedule (live prd 2026-09-14: `storage-sync-cronjob` scheduled 00:10:00Z, last success 00:13:25Z), so the threshold carries a margin of a few hours, and every mirror run ends, succeeded or failed, within a bound inside that margin. Two consecutive missed nights fire, a few hours after the second failed run, and so does a mirror that has never succeeded. `postgres-backup` is not added to it.
items.rationale: The rule is deployed live in the prd Prometheus release: `GET /api/v1/rules?type=alert` against the running `prometheus-prd-server` pod shows group `s3-mirror`, rule `S3MirrorStale`, expression matching the plan exactly (`time() - max by (namespace, cronjob) (kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{...} or kube_cronjob_created{...}) > 52 * 3600`), `state: inactive`, `health: ok` — loaded and evaluating cleanly, not yet firing (correct: the CronJob was created ~20 minutes before the check, nowhere near the 52 h bound). The margin arithmetic (48 h + run-length + DST + evaluation lag < 52 h) is walked night-by-night over 400 nights by `tests/test_prometheus_s3_mirror_alert.py`, which `kc project test` runs. `postgres-backup` does not appear in the rule's selector.
evidence: live: `kubectl -n prometheus-prd exec deploy/prometheus-prd-server -- wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/api/v1/rules?type=alert` — group `s3-mirror`, rule `S3MirrorStale`, `state: inactive`, `health: ok`, 2026-09-14 15:42 UTC
HelmCharts `configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:131-146` — the rule as deployed
HelmCharts `tests/test_prometheus_s3_mirror_alert.py` — walks both edges over 400 nights

items.description: The runbook beside `openbao.md` covers restoring a bucket from the mirror (whole, or single objects and earlier versions from the archive), writing into the production bucket with the app's own key. It also covers reading the mirror with no cluster, from the Drive login and the Roboform-held crypt password and salt. It names where each credential it needs actually lives (ruling B2): the app's key pair in the Terraform-written Secret in the app's namespace (HelmCharts `terraform-modules/s3-storage/main.tf:62-72`), `backup-reader`'s key in the Terraform-written Secret in `storage-prd`, the crypt password and salt in OpenBao `eso/prd/storage/prd/s3-mirror` and Roboform, and the scratch user the drill creates on dev Ceph. Reading any of those values is the operator's keystroke or needs the operator's permission, and the drill reads the live bucket with `backup-reader`'s read-only key, never the app's.
items.rationale: `docs/runbooks/s3-mirror.md` is written and pushed, beside `openbao.md` as required. It has the mirror layout, a credential table (ruling B2), §2 whole-bucket restore (suspends the CronJob, `rclone copy`s `current/` then replays archive folders newest-first, verifies with `rclone check --one-way --download`, resumes the CronJob), §3 single object/earlier version, §4 no-cluster read (Drive login + Roboform crypt values via `rclone obscure`), and §5 the restore drill with a drill-log placeholder. Every command is framed as the operator's keystroke; credential provenance matches the description exactly.
evidence: Ansible `docs/runbooks/s3-mirror.md`, full read 2026-09-14 post-push

items.description: The provider's reader user and bucket-grant behaviour carry unit tests in the `internal/s3storage` package's existing style, plus acceptance tests that skip without `TF_ACC`. The tests `kc project test` runs include the no-reader case V08 rests on: a resource asking for the grant on a provider with no reader configured grants nothing and plans no change.
items.rationale: `internal/s3storage/resource_test.go` carries `TestStorageWithoutAskPlansNoChange`, `TestStorageGrantWithoutReaderIsInert` (the no-reader case) and `TestStorageGrantWithReader`; `internal/s3storage/client_test.go` and `internal/s3reader/client_test.go` cover the client behaviour (`TestClientGrantReader`, `TestClientRevokeReader`, `TestClientReaderGranted`, `TestDiffBuckets`, etc.) against `httptest`. `internal/s3reader/resource_acc_test.go::TestAccS3Reader_basic` and `internal/s3storage/resource_acc_test.go::TestAccS3Storage_readerGrant`/`TestAccS3Storage_basic` are the acceptance pair, gated on `TF_ACC`. `kc project test` for HomelabTerraformProvider is green per the dispatch's established sweep (does not set `TF_ACC`, so only the unit suite ran); the acceptance pair stays close-out A2.
